content: Voglibose is an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor that is specifically utilized to reduce postprandial blood glucose levels in individuals diagnosed with diabetes mellitus. This medication is manufactured in India by Ranbaxy Laboratories and is marketed under the trade name Volix. Additionally, Glenmark Pharmaceuticals produces voglibose under the brand name Vocarb. Diabetes mellitus is a chronic metabolic condition characterized by persistent hyperglycemia, which arises due to either a relative or absolute deficiency of insulin or the presence of insulin resistance. Postprandial hyperglycemia (PPHG) refers to elevated blood glucose levels following a meal, primarily caused by an impaired first-phase insulin secretion. Alpha-glucosidase inhibitors, such as voglibose, function by delaying the absorption of glucose in the intestines. This mechanism helps to prevent a rapid increase in blood glucose levels after meals. Within this pharmacological class, there are three primary agents: acarbose, miglitol, and voglibose. Voglibose is the most recent addition to this class and demonstrates superior efficacy and a more favorable side effect profile compared to acarbose and miglitol. Numerous clinical trials have validated the effectiveness of voglibose in managing postprandial hyperglycemia. Furthermore, research has established that postprandial hyperglycemia, rather than fasting plasma glucose (FPG), serves as a more significant marker for cardiovascular complications associated with diabetes. Therefore, controlling postprandial hyperglycemia is critical in the comprehensive management of diabetes, and voglibose is specifically indicated for this purpose. Sun Pharmaceuticals has introduced voglibose in 0.2 mg and 0.3 mg formulations under the brand name Volibo.
